correctness.rationale: The primary shellability theorem arxiv:2603.23155 identifies the unique degree n-4 and rank B=binom(n-2p,2)-(2p^2+p-1). The Alexander dual consists of vertex sets whose nonedge-induced graph has maximum degree one; equivariant Alexander duality supplies the ambient sign twist. Rotations of order >=3 admit no nonempty fixed dual faces; half-turns contribute the m antipodal pair faces. Reflection axes yield isolated orbit terms plus cancellations at vertex or edge axes, giving the exact formulas; the invariant ranks follow averaging. The independent *earlier* published proofs directly validate the same face/orbit argument, and exact algebraic sign conversion identifies each candidate class with prior formulas for all parameters. Independent small-parameter tests check equality for p=2..6 and all prescribed axis parities; these are ancillary to the symbolic identity.
